text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

All newspapers: The central Bank Negara said not many banks were over-exposed in loans to the property sector and that it would take a patient approach in letting banks meet its 20 percent lending limit to the sector.
-- Timber company Raspand Sdn Bhd is suing the Sabah state government for 113.9 million ringgit in damages for alleged wrongful detention of its logs.

-- Initial public offers of infrastructure and manufacturing companies will not fall under the lending guidelines for purchases of stocks and shares announced recently by Bank Negara, said its Deputy Governor Fong Weng Phak.

-- Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said lavish spending and misuse of public funds by sports associations, non-governmental organisations and welfare foundations have not stopped.
-- YTL Power International Bhd will be able to build a 5,000 megawatt power plant using proceeds from its flotation exercise, said company managing director Francis Yeoh.
